title: SEC-01: Unauthenticated disclosure of draft material metadata
description: Four administrative search GET handlers do not authenticate callers and are outside the /admin proxy matcher. Materials and group-photo queries omit published-only predicates, disclosing draft titles, IDs and relationships; group-photo responses also include status. Source code and a disposable fixture GET harness confirm the handler-level flow. No production HTTP or database query was performed; no body/file/credential disclosure is claimed.
root_cause: GET in src/app/api/admin/group-photos/search/route.ts does not require administrator authorization before querying and returning draft metadata, allowing unauthenticated disclosure.
intended_behavior: Administrative search should allow a verified administrator to find both published and draft materials while refusing anonymous callers before database access; public material pages hide drafts.

trace.description: Accepts request query without reading a session or checking administrator identity.
Matcher covers /admin/:path*, so /api/admin/group-photos/search is outside its authentication guard.
Queries material id, title and status, filtering group_photo/search but not requiring published status.
Queries linked person names for the returned material IDs.
Serializes the grouped draft metadata as a JSON response.

conditions.description: Request reaches the application API without an additional infrastructure authentication layer; no NGINX configuration was supplied.
A draft group_photo matching the query exists. Related materials endpoint leaks matching draft metadata as well.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated visitor able to send read requests to the application.
payloads: GET /api/admin/group-photos/search?q=Audit (no Cookie; isolated fixture host only)
GET /api/admin/materials/search?q=Audit (no Cookie; isolated fixture host only)
instructions: In an isolated non-production copy create disposable Audit Draft material fixtures.
Request the administrative search GET without a cookie.
Compare returned draft metadata against the public material page publication boundary. The performed harness used a fixture DB rather than a live HTTP application.
execution.expected_result: Before the fix the handler returns matching draft IDs/titles/relationships and group-photo status. After the fix anonymous requests receive 401/403 before database access.

remediation.strategy: Require a valid, existing administrator through a shared guard at the beginning of all four admin search handlers; retain draft search for authenticated editors. Add negative authentication checks and verify zero DB reads on rejection.

likelihood.reason: Unauthenticated GET and predictable endpoint; infrastructure may add separate restrictions.

impact.reason: Limited disclosure of unpublished editorial metadata, without material bodies or credentials.

confidence.reason: Independent source review confirmed matcher and predicates; original GET executed with a disposable fixture DB. Real production data, NGINX and HTTP routing were not tested.

title: SEC-02: Copied session JWT survives logout and password change
description: JWT sessions expire seven days after issue but are not bound to server revocation state. Logout deletes only the current browser cookie; password change updates only the password hash. Someone already holding a valid copy can retain administrator access until the original expiry unless the signing secret is externally rotated. A disposable-key fixture harness confirmed token acceptance after logout; password-change behavior was traced statically.
root_cause: getSession in src/lib/session.ts does not check server-side revocation or password/session version, allowing a previously copied token to remain usable after logout or password change.
intended_behavior: Administrators should be able to end a session or revoke compromised access on password change, rather than merely deleting a local copy of the credential.

trace.description: Issues a signed JWT with userId/role and the seven-day expiration constant.
Changes only the stored bcrypt password hash without invalidating outstanding tokens.
Logout removes only the cookie from the current client cookie store.
A copied token still passes signature/expiry validation without querying revocation state.
A still-valid signed token is accepted for access to administrative routes.

conditions.description: Attacker already possesses an unexpired copy of a genuine administrator JWT. No independent token-theft or forgery path was established.
The signing secret has not been rotated, and no additional infrastructure control independently rejects the caller.
Access persists only for the remaining lifetime up to seven days from issue, not seven new days after logout/reset.

execution.attacker_perspective: Holder of a previously copied valid session credential.
payloads: GET /admin/materials with Cookie: session=<DISPOSABLE_FIXTURE_JWT_ONLY>; non-production fixture environment only
instructions: Issue a JWT using the actual session module with a disposable fixture signing key and cookie store.
Save a copy, invoke deleteSession, and verify the fixture cookie store is empty.
Restore the copied token in the fixture store and call getSession: it accepts the user again.
A future staging-only test can check an old second-client session after a fixture account password change; no production token or password was used.
execution.expected_result: Before remediation the copied JWT remains accepted until its original exp. After server-side revocation or password-version invalidation it is rejected while a fresh valid session works.

remediation.strategy: Implement revocable server sessions or enforce a sessionVersion on protected access and increment it on password change/global revocation. For revoking only the current session on logout use a per-session identifier/store. Ensure existing-user/admin checks occur in the shared authorization boundary.

likelihood.reason: Requires prior compromise of a valid session, not anonymous access.

impact.reason: Retains administrator privileges after an attempted account/session recovery.

confidence.reason: Independently reviewed issuance, password update, logout and validators; isolated execution confirmed logout-copy acceptance. Password-update invalidation absence is static; live production not tested.
